description: d3's symlog transform is `Math.sign(x) * Math.log1p(Math.abs(x / c))`, and every part of that line is load-bearing. `log1p` and `ln(1 + t)` are the same function and not the same arithmetic — adding one to a small number throws away the low bits before the logarithm sees them — so a domain near zero places a value one or two units in the last place away from upstream. The first scale is that case: its domain is `[0.1, 0.30000000000000004]`, where this engine put 0.2 at `…4051715` and upstream puts it at `…4051665`. `Math.abs(x / c)` rather than `abs(x) / c` is the second: they agree for a positive constant and part company for a negative one, which the third scale uses. `Math.sign` being zero at zero is the third, which is why a symlog of `-0` is `-0`. Written out through a text mark rather than left to the marks' positions, because the difference is in the last digits and a coordinate is rounded long before it reaches the page. The engine had this rule transcribed three times, in the positional scale, in the colour-ramp transform and in the expression `pan`/`zoom` functions, and only the last of the three was right.

text.signal: 'negC ' + scale('negC', datum.w) + '  bigC ' + scale('bigC', datum.w) + '  back ' + invert('bigC', 40)
